stem: Simon is an 8-week-old infant with fever (38.9°C), poor feeding, and irritability. He is otherwise well appearing and has no focal examination findings. Which ONE of the following is the most appropriate management plan, pending any results?
explanation: An infant aged 8 weeks with fever is in the high-risk group for serious bacterial infection and requires prompt parenteral antibiotics after appropriate sepsis workup. Cefotaxime is an appropriate empiric choice in this age group. Discharge or oral therapy is not appropriate.
rationale: Fever in infants under 3 months warrants urgent assessment for serious bacterial infection and empiric IV antibiotics after cultures/urine testing.

optionExplanations.A: Unsafe in a febrile 8-week-old infant because serious bacterial infection must be excluded.
optionExplanations.B: Observation alone is insufficient; this infant needs full evaluation and empiric treatment.
optionExplanations.C: Oral antibiotics are inadequate for possible sepsis in this age group.
optionExplanations.D: Ampicillin and gentamicin is a common neonatal regimen, but cefotaxime is the better empiric option here.
optionExplanations.E: Correct: broad-spectrum IV cover for a febrile young infant pending investigation results.

RR 30/min
